The General Colonization Law allows foreigners to gain titles to any land they wish to settle that isn't within 20 leagues of the border of another country or within 10 leagues of the coast. Settlers are be exempt from taxes for ten years. Most individuals are restricted to a total of 11 square leagues of land. Of them, 6 square leagues can be for grazing animals, 1 square league can be irrigable land and 4 square leagues can be non-irrigable. New towns are given an additional 4 square leagues of land for public use. Empresarios are granted more personal land. For every 100 families settled, the empresario can receive 5 sitios of grazing land and 5 labores of farmland. The law doesn't require settlers to be Mexican citizens or catholic although citizens are given preference in land grants and federal laws prohibit all religions except Catholicism. Land grants are made from available public land.

\n\nAgainst all expectations, General Santa Anna has led Mexico to triumph. After routing the initial American invasion, he pursued the fleeing attackers and drove them back across the border. Following his initial success, Santa Anna executed a string of victories against the disorganized Americans, thus uniting the Mexican people behind him. Now that the Americans have finally sued for peace, he has returned to Mexico City as a revered hero, and his rivals have gone into hiding. Making use his enduring popularity, General Santa has awarded himself with the title of "Most Serene Highness" and announced that he will serve as president for life. For now, his position is secure, but it is likely that, as his popularity wanes and his cruelty comes to bear on the people, he will once again be deposed.

\n\nThe American army under General Winfield Scott has soundly defeated General Santa Anna. After facing many humiliating retreats and even losing his prosthetic leg to the enemy at the Battle of Cerro Gordo, General Santa Anna is now widely despised and ridiculed. He has scuttled away into exile in Kingston, Jamaica, with his tail between his legs. Despite his long record of failures, betrayals and previous exiles, General Santa Anna still has some remaining allies in Mexico City. Though he is hated by the Mexican people, this bungling despot may yet return in the years to come.

\n\nThe regime of President Mariano Paredes has fallen. Even before the invasion, the government was so unpopular that multiple states denied it taxes and conscripts to fight the widespread unrest. The Organic Bases of 1843, meant to strengthen unitarianism and empower the central authority in Mexico City only further eroded its support. General José Miguel Salas has put forth the Plan of la Ciudadela, which has two aims: Firstly, the return of the 1824 federalist constitution, ending unitarianism. Secondly, the return of General Santa Anna to lead Mexico to victory against the United States. With General Salas' almost effortless triumph over President Paredes, General Santa Anna has landed in Veracruz, returning from exile to lead Mexico once again.

\n\nAfter toppling President Bustamante with the Bases of Tacubaya in 1841, General Santa Anna attempted to rule Mexico with an iron fist. Instituting the Organic Bases, a new constitution that gave the unitary government in Mexico City even more authority, he hoped to put an end to the unrest. It was, however, not to be: The new policies led to the exact opposite outcome. New revolts to restore federalism flared up in Yucatán and Tabasco, while many governors simply began refusing to contribute to the national army or send taxes they collected to the government. This has led to General Santa Anna becoming immensely unpopular and beleaguered on all sides. Seeing the writing on the wall, he has fled Mexico for Cuba. He did so just in time, it seems, as angry crowds have exumed his amputated leg and dragged it across the capital.
